dominant_strengths: Confident headline scale and clean sans-serif type set a credible, developer-native tone against the dark canvas
Two-column product split (Warp/Oz) communicates a clear product taxonomy with parallel CTAs and matching screenshot crops
Screenshots are detailed and authentic, signaling craft and giving immediate visceral proof of the agentic workflow
dominant_weaknesses: Purple gradient washes behind both screenshots feel generic AI-SaaS, undermining Warp's terminal-native distinctiveness
Top announcement bar is centered and floating awkwardly above the nav, creating two competing horizontal bands
Symmetric dual-hero dilutes focus — neither Warp nor Oz dominates, weakening the 'agentic development environment' claim
fix_priorities: Establish hierarchy between Warp and Oz (size, order, or staggered reveal) instead of mirrored equal columns
Replace the lavender gradient backdrops with a more terminal-authentic treatment (deep grid, glow, or code particles)
Integrate the announcement banner into the nav row or anchor it flush to reduce vertical fragmentation
Tighten screenshot framing — current crops show too much chrome and reduce legibility of the core agent UI
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral clarity leads via clear CTAs and product split, visceral impact is moderate due to stocky gradients, and reflective payoff is muted because the positioning feels familiar.
rationale.intent_fit: It functions as a competent devtools landing page but doesn't visually embody 'agentic environment' beyond stating it in the headline.
